repos.readme_text:
# Chronicles of the Realm · 江山时序

English · 简体中文 (Chinese) · 繁體中文 (Traditional Chinese) · 日本語 (Japanese)

**An Interactive Historical Atlas of China from the Warring States (403 BCE) to the Present — Scrub Through Time, Trace Ancient Cities, and Walk in the Footsteps of History** [**Play Live Demo (English UI) → https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en**](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en) *The story behind it (in Chinese): [From textbook maps to 1k GitHub stars](https://deanchen.me/history/atlas/2026/10/25/jiangshan-map-story.html)*

--- ## Why It's Fun to Explore Have you ever wondered while reading Chinese history or classical poetry: - *"Where exactly on today's map are Jiankang (the Six Dynasties capital), Huangzhou (where Su Dongpo composed the Red Cliffs Rhapsody in exile), Languan Pass in the Qinling Mountains (where Han Yu halted his horse in the snow), or Zhuxianzhen (Yue Fei's northern campaign frontier)?"* - *"How many names did Chang'an hold across two millennia, and what pivotal events unfolded on that soil?"* - *"How did the realm evolve step by step—from the Partition of Jin and the Seven Warring States at the opening of Sima Guang's Zizhi Tongjian (403 BCE), Qin's unification campaigns, Emperor Wu of Han opening the Hexi Corridor, High Tang's Four Garrisons of Anxi, and Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan jurisdiction over Tibet, to Zeng Jize's recovery of Ili (1881 CE) and the 20th-century shift from the 'Begonia Leaf' (秋海棠) map to the 'Rooster' (雄鸡) map?"* **Chronicles of the Realm (`jiangshan-map`)** brings together **2,400+ years** of Chinese history across **18 historical periods** into a single interactive parchment atlas—featuring **multi-stage territorial and prefecture snapshots**, **ancient cities**, **strategic mountain passes**, **poetic and battlefield landmarks**, **chronological milestones**, and **reigning monarchs & imperial eras**. No heavy print atlases required—just drag the timeline and click any city to travel through space and time. --- ### Feature 1: Scrub the Timeline to Watch Realms Rise & Fall, Track Monarchs, and Compare Ancient & Modern Borders - **Multi-Polity Confrontations on a Single Canvas**: From the Seven Warring States (Qin, Chu, Qi, Yan, Zhao, Wei, Han) alongside Zhou, Yue, Ba-Shu, Zhongshan, and Yiqu, to the Three Kingdoms warlords (Yuan Shao, Cao Cao, Liu Bei, Sun Quan, Gongsun's Liaodong), Northern & Southern Dynasties, Five Dynasties & Ten Kingdoms, and Song, Liao, Western Xia, Dali, Jin, and the Mongols—all rendered side-by-side in high-contrast traditional parchment hues. Hover over any polity in the bottom-left legend to highlight its territory, or click to open that polity's profile (lifespan, capitals and a short history) and zoom to its territory. - **Multi-Stage Territorial Evolution & Dashed "Ghost Boundary Diffs"**: At every major territorial milestone—such as Qin's conquest of Ba-Shu (316 BCE), Yan General Qin Kai's expansion into Liaodong (300 BCE), Ma

# /last30days English | [Français](README.fr.md) | [Deutsch](README.de.md) | [Español](README.es.md) | [Português (Brasil)](README.pt-BR.md) | [日本語](README.ja.md) | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) | [العربية](README.ar.md)



**An AI agent-led search engine scored by upvotes, likes, and real money - not editors.** This README tracks the current v4 pipeline. The runtime skill spec lives in [skills/last30days/SKILL.md](skills/last30days/SKILL.md), which is the source of truth for the latest command and setup behavior. **Claude Code (recommended — auto-updates via marketplace):** ``` /plugin marketplace add mvanhorn/last30days-skill /plugin install last30days ``` **Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, or any of 50+ [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) hosts:** ``` npx skills add mvanhorn/last30days-skill -g ``` (`-g` installs globally for your user, available across all projects. Drop it to scope per-project.) More install options (claude.ai web, OpenClaw, manual) in the [Install](#install) section below. Zero config. Reddit, HN, Polymarket, and GitHub work immediately, and so do patent filings and careers pages when your topic is a company. Run it once and the setup wizard unlocks X, YouTube, TikTok, arXiv, Techmeme, and more in 30 seconds. --- Reddit upvotes. X likes. YouTube transcripts. TikTok engagement. Polymarket odds backed by real money and insider information. That's millions of people voting with their attention and their wallets every day. /last30days searches all of it in parallel, scores it by what real people actually engage with, and an AI agent judge synthesizes it into one brief. Google aggregates editors. /last30days searches people. You can't get this search anywhere else because no single AI has access to all of it. Google search doesn't touch Reddit comments or X posts. ChatGPT has a deal with Reddit but can't search X or TikTok. Gemini has YouTube but not Reddit. Claude has none of them natively. Each platform is a walled garden with its own API, its own tokens, its own auth. But you can bring your own keys and browser sessions, and suddenly an AI agent can search all of them at once, score them against each other, and tell you what actually matters. That's the unlock. Not one better search engine. A dozen disconnected platforms, bridged by an agent. ``` /last30days Peter Steinberger ``` You have a meeting tomorrow. You Google them. You get their LinkedIn from 2023. /last30days gives you what they're actually doing this month: joined OpenAI to work on Codex, fighting Anthropic's ban on third-party agents, shipping 23 PRs at 85% merge rate, building "LobsterOS" for cross-device agent control, and r/ClaudeCode hit 569 upvotes debating whether he's a hero or "insufferable." Scattered across X posts, Reddit threads, YouTube transcripts, and GitHub commits. None of it was on Google. ## Why this exists I built it to keep up in AI. Everything changes every day and the Reddit and X nerds are always on top of it first. I needed better prompts, and the training data was always months behind

repos.readme_text:
#
🎻 PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing
Yiwen Song1, Yale Song1, Tomas Pfister1, and Jinsung Yoon1
1Google Cloud AI Research


PaperOrchestra is a multi-agent framework for automated AI research paper writing. It flexibly transforms unconstrained pre-writing materials (ideas and experimental logs) into submission-ready LaTeX manuscripts, including comprehensive literature synthesis and generated visuals, such as plots and conceptual diagrams. Acting like an orchestrated team of specialized agents, it handles outline generation, literature review, section writing, content refinement, and plotting to close the gap between raw research materials and submission ready papers.
## Key Features - **Multi-Agent Pipeline**: Orchestrates specialized agents (Outline, Literature Review, Section Writing, Content Refinement, Plotting) for end-to-end paper generation. - **Comprehensive Literature Synthesis**: Automatically searches, prioritizes, and integrates relevant literature into the manuscript. - **Visuals Generation**: Generates plots and supports the inclusion of conceptual diagrams. - **LaTeX Automation**: Produces submission-ready LaTeX manuscripts adhering to target conference templates. ## Installation 1. **Environment Setup**: The project relies on a Conda environment named `paper_orchestra`. You can set up a similar environment with Python 3.11 and install the required dependencies. ```bash conda create -n paper_orchestra python=3.11 conda activate paper_orchestra pip install -r requirements.txt ``` 2. **Environment Variables**: Create a `.env` file in the root of the project and add your API keys: ```env # Add keys if you have them, otherwise leave them empty # You need to specify related keys if you want to use the model # For example, if you want to use Gemini models, you need to specify either VERTEX_AI_PROJECT and VERTEX_AI_LOCATION, or GEMINI_API_KEY # If you want to use OpenAI models, you need to specify OPENAI_API_KEY SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY=your_semantic_scholar_api_key OPENAI_API_KEY=your_openai_api_key VERTEX_AI_PROJECT=your_vertex_ai_project VERTEX_AI_LOCATION=your_vertex_ai_location GEMINI_API_KEY=your_gemini_api_key # if you want to run demo and send emails to yourself at the end, set these 2 fields as well SMTP_EMAIL=your_email SMTP_PASSWORD=your_password ``` ## Dataset The dataset used for paper generation is **not included** in this code repository. It will be released separately at a later date. Once available, you should download the dataset and place it under the `datasets/` directory. ## Usage You can run the paper generation pipeline using the provided bash script or directly via the Python CLI. ### Using the Bash Script ```bash ./paper_writing_cli.sh ``` ### Using the Python CLI directly ```bash python paper_writing_cli.py \ --raw_materials_dir /path_to_your_raw_materials/ \ --latex_template_dir /path_to_your_latex_template/ \ --output_dir /path_to_your_output_folder/ \ --use_plotting true ``` ### Key Arguments * `--raw_materials_dir`: (Required) Directory containing the raw materials (e.g., idea and experimental log). * `--latex_template_dir`: (Required) Directory containing the LaTeX template (e.g., `templates/cvpr2025`). * `--output_dir`: Directory to output the generated paper. If not specified, an automatic folder with a timestamp is created. * `--use_plotting`: Enable the plotting agent workflow to generate figures from code (Default: `False`). * `--writer_model_name`: LLM for writer and literature agents. * `--reflection_model_name`: LLM for reflection agents. ### Interactive Demo We provide an i

repos.description: Local video editor for coding agents: 42 FFmpeg tools with a machine-readable contract and an MCP server, for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex. Cut, captions, reframe, loudness, platform exports. No cloud, no API keys.
repos.readme_text:
Give your coding agent a video editor.
Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or any MCP client edits your footage with local FFmpeg, then checks its own output.
No cloud · No API keys · Python standard library

Website · Quick start · Demos · Tools · MCP · npm

```bash npx ffmpeg-skill ```

caption.py --animate pop --karaoke
fit.py --aspect 9:16 --fit crop

silence.py --threshold -35
loudness.py -I -14 --tp -1
Left half is the input, right half is what the command produced. **[Every before/after demo, with the exact command under each one →](docs/demos.md)** — all of it built by `python3 demos/build.py`, so you can rebuild every frame of it yourself. The footage is synthetic (FFmpeg's own test sources) except in three demos, `reframe_talk`, `filler_en` and `pauses_en`, which use two AI-generated clips of people who do not exist ([demos/footage/](demos/footage/README.md)). `ffmpeg-skill` is an [Agent Skill](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/agent-skills) for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and any agent that reads `SKILL.md`. It teaches the agent a fixed workflow (probe → edit losslessly where possible → check → verify) and ships **42 tools** that do the actual work with `ffmpeg` / `ffprobe`: cut, join, silence removal, fit to duration and aspect, captions and karaoke, overlays and motion graphics, HDR → SDR and LUTs, audio clean-up and typed dynamics, sync with drift correction, multicam, loudness, delivery checks, whole-edit project rendering, batch folders. Every tool is also callable as an MCP tool (`tools/list` advertises a core 12 by default to keep client context small, with `FFMPEG_SKILL_MCP_
